## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Serīsakapetavatthu* (Pv 37) is a narrative poem preserved in the *Petavatthu* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The story concerns a *deva* (god) who encounters a group of merchants stranded and lost in the desert, instructing them on the karmic fruition of wholesome deeds and the importance of upholding ethical precepts [SuttaCentral]. In a thematic analysis of Buddhist resolve (*adhiṭṭhāna*), the text is cited for its use of the verbal imperative *adhiṭṭhahātha* in the admonition *dhammānuyogañca adhiṭṭhahātha* ("resolutely determine on the practice of the Dhamma") [Lim Hwee San 2009].

A full parallel to the text exists in the *Vimānavatthu* as the *Serīsakavimānavatthu* (Vv 84) [SuttaCentral]. This direct correspondence is corroborated by DharmaNexus text-reuse computations, which identify virtually identical shared verse material across segments §1.1–55.1 [DharmaNexus]. The text is also explicitly connected to the *Saṅkhapālajātaka* (Ja 524) and the *Vidhurajātaka* (Ja 546) [SuttaCentral], both of which share a sequence of verses (§22.1–24.2) with the text [DharmaNexus]. Additional Pali-internal reuse connects this discourse with other *Petavatthu* texts—such as the *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17), *Ambasakkarapetavatthu* (Pv 36), and *Nandakapetavatthu* (Pv 38)—as well as extensive commentary excerpts in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan works, including Prajñākaramati's *Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā* and the Tibetan *Lokaprajñapti*, alongside minor phrase matches in the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* [DharmaNexus].
